subject: Suite wall-time swings ~40x between identical runs — TIMEOUT rows in the release snapshot may be load artifacts
description:
OBSERVED s321, not yet explained. The t/op dir was measured twice on the same commit, same machine, same runner:
  - attempt 1: --jobs 3, 58 of 218 files in 83 min  (~0.7 files/min)
  - attempt 2: --jobs 4, 163 files in ~5 min        (~33 files/min)
Both on an otherwise idle box as far as I could tell; jobs 3->4 cannot explain 40x.

WHY IT MATTERS: the runner's per-file cap is wall-clock (--timeout 150). If a run can be 40x slower for reasons we do not understand, then TIMEOUT rows in docs/perl-suite-run.tsv are not necessarily statements about PCL — they may be statements about the machine at that moment. The release snapshot currently carries 6 TIMEOUT rows across the ten non-op dirs. Same family as #176 (a timeout silently becoming a fact about the product).

*** s333: HYPOTHESIS (a')-ish CONFIRMED FOR THE SISTER SYMPTOM — SYSTEM-WIDE MEMORY PRESSURE. ***
A full perl-tests sweep failed #204's gate with "LOST ref.t -5 (184 -> 179)", TOTAL -1.  An
immediate re-run of the SAME TREE was clean with ref.t 186+18.  The user suggested runaway
memory; journalctl confirms it directly:

  Aug 03 02:04:43 kernel: systemd-journal invoked oom-killer: ...
  Aug 03 02:04:43 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 432648 (Isolated Web Co)
                          total-vm:4239956kB, anon-rss:1054148kB

System-wide OOM (no cgroup cap), fired while run 1 was executing ref.t (file 84/108, 91 s;
run ended 02:08:15).  Run 2 started 02:08 with that ~1 GB freed and was clean.  CONTROL: 8
heavy files incl. ref.t at --jobs 8 with headroom give ref.t 186+18 and 8.9 GB MINIMUM
AVAILABLE — concurrency alone does not reproduce it.  ref.t is the sensitive file because it
forks 23 fresh_perl_is/runperl children (each a fresh transpile + SBCL); under memory
pressure those get starved and fail ROWS without aborting the file, which is exactly the
shape that survives sweep-diff's UNSTABLE filter and lands in LOST.

CONSEQUENCE: the box is a 13 GB desktop shared with a browser; "otherwise idle" was never
verified in s321 either.  Before trusting any wall-time or LOST verdict, RECORD THE MACHINE
STATE WITH THE RUN.  Concrete: sample MemAvailable during the sweep/runner and print the
minimum next to the verdict, and check `journalctl -k | grep oom-killer` for the run window.
Proposed gate policy in docs/opus5-review-requests-s333.md §4 (option 0 = record it,
option 2 = re-run a LOST file once at --jobs 1 before failing).  #128 (leaking pl2cl --server,
caught at 4.95 GB) is the same failure mode with a cause inside our own tree.

STILL OPEN from s321: cold-cache vs warm-cache timing for the 40x itself; per-file elapsed
time in the tsv so a TIMEOUT can be told from a near-timeout.
